Holcim Liban SAL Enters Insolvency, Disrupting Lebanon’s Construction Sector

Holcim Liban SAL, a major player in Lebanon’s construction materials sector, has entered insolvency proceedings, sending immediate shockwaves through its operations and the broader industry. The company, which has been a primary supplier of cement and other essential building materials, confirmed on Thursday that it is unable to meet its financial obligations and is currently undergoing court-supervised administration.

Operations at Holcim Liban SAL’s main cement plant in Chekka have been significantly curtailed, with reports of reduced production shifts and halted deliveries to numerous construction sites across the country. Employees at the facility described uncertainty about their future, with union representatives warning that up to 400 jobs could be at risk if the situation is not resolved swiftly.

“We are doing our best to maintain essential operations, but the pressure on staff is tremendous,” said a senior manager at Holcim Liban SAL who requested anonymity. “Our immediate focus is on stabilizing the company’s finances and ensuring safety at our sites.”

Industry analysts say the insolvency is likely to exacerbate Lebanon’s ongoing construction slowdown. According to the Lebanese Contractors Association, cement prices have already spiked by 12% in the past week amid mounting supply concerns. “The insolvency of a company of this scale further strains an industry already under immense stress from economic instability and currency fluctuations,” said Marwan Haddad, a Beirut-based industry analyst.

Local construction firms such as Atlas BuildCo and Cedar Structures report delays in ongoing projects as they scramble to secure alternative sources of cement. The Lebanese Ministry of Industry has called for an emergency meeting to assess the impact on infrastructure projects.

As of Friday, Holcim Liban SAL remains under court protection, with creditors awaiting an initial restructuring proposal. The future of the company—and its workforce—remains uncertain as insolvency proceedings continue to unfold.
